introduction: The Dynamic Complexity Assessment system replaces static model-tier assignments with a lightweight, LLM-driven complexity signal that upgrades model selection only when task complexity warrants it, ensuring quality-critical tasks always run at full strength while avoiding unnecessary cost for simple work.

glossary.ARCHETYPE_REGISTRY: Registry in archetypes.py mapping archetype names to their default model tier and variant assignments.
glossary.AssessedComplexity: Frozen dataclass embedded in TriageResult (nightshift/fix_pipeline.py) containing tier, variant, confidence, and rationale from the nightshift triage model.
glossary.AssessmentManager: Class in engine/engine.py that coordinates complexity assessment for nodes, integrating ComplexityAssessor with dispatch logic.
glossary.AssessmentResult: Frozen dataclass returned by ComplexityAssessor.assess(), containing recommended_tier, recommended_variant, confidence, and rationale.
glossary.ComplexityAssessor: Class in core/complexity.py responsible for calling the Anthropic LLM to assess task complexity and return a structured recommendation.
glossary.ComplexityAssessor.assess(): Async method on ComplexityAssessor that sends a prompt to the configured LLM and returns an AssessmentResult.
glossary.ComplexityRecommendation: Protocol (shared interface) satisfied by both AssessmentResult and AssessedComplexity (via adapter), accepted by apply_assessment().
glossary.DispatchManager: Class in engine/dispatch.py that manages the dispatch of nodes to agents, including complexity assessment via AssessmentManager.
glossary.EscalationLadder: Object representing the ordered sequence of model tiers/variants a node may escalate through during retries, with a configured starting_tier and starting_variant.
glossary.ModelTier: Enum in the codebase representing model capability tiers: SIMPLE, STANDARD, and ADVANCED.
glossary.RoutingConfig: Pydantic configuration model in core/config.py under the [routing] section, containing assessor_model and confidence_threshold among other routing settings.
glossary.TriageResult: Dataclass in nightshift/fix_pipeline.py representing the structured output of the nightshift triage model, extended to include assessed_complexity.
glossary.VARIANT_ORDER: Ordered sequence of model variants from spec #14: fast (0) < standard (1) < extended (2), used for variant upgrade comparisons.
glossary.apply_assessment: Function in core/complexity.py that enforces upgrade-only semantics when applying a ComplexityRecommendation to a base tier/variant.
glossary.apply_assessment(): Function in core/complexity.py that enforces upgrade-only semantics when applying a ComplexityRecommendation to a base tier/variant.
glossary.archetype: A named agent role (e.g. coder, reviewer, verifier, maintainer) that determines the base model tier and dispatch behaviour.
glossary.assess_node: Async method on AssessmentManager that orchestrates complexity assessment for a single node and returns an EscalationLadder.
glossary.assessed_complexity_to_recommendation: Adapter function in core/complexity.py that converts an AssessedComplexity to an AssessmentResult for use with apply_assessment().
glossary.assessed_complexity_to_recommendation(): Adapter function in core/complexity.py that converts an AssessedComplexity to an AssessmentResult for use with apply_assessment().
glossary.assessor_model: Configuration value in RoutingConfig specifying the Anthropic model ID used for complexity assessment (default: claude-haiku-4-5).
glossary.base_tier: The configured floor tier for a given archetype/mode before any assessment upgrade is applied.
glossary.base_variant: The configured floor variant for a given archetype/mode before any assessment upgrade is applied.
glossary.coder_reviewer.py: Nightshift orchestrator module (nightshift/coder_reviewer.py) that coordinates coder and reviewer nodes for the fix pipeline.
glossary.confidence_threshold: Configuration value (float, 0.0–1.0) in RoutingConfig; assessments with confidence below this value are ignored and base tier/variant is used.
glossary.error_tracker: Dict in the dispatch layer that stores per-node failure information including the last error string used as previous_failure.
glossary.fix_pipeline.py: Module (nightshift/fix_pipeline.py) containing TriageResult, AssessedComplexity, and related nightshift data structures.
glossary.is_explicitly_configured: Helper function that walks config resolution layers 1–3 to determine whether a tier has been explicitly set for a given archetype/mode.
glossary.mode: An optional sub-mode within an archetype (e.g. fix, pre-review, audit-review) that further refines model tier selection.
glossary.nightshift: The automated overnight fix pipeline that triages issues and dispatches coder/reviewer nodes.
glossary.node_body: The full text content of a task graph Node, representing the work to be assessed for complexity.
glossary.pre_assessed: Optional AssessedComplexity parameter passed to assess_node() from the nightshift orchestrator, bypassing the Haiku LLM call when present.
glossary.prepare_launch: Method on DispatchManager in engine/dispatch.py responsible for extracting node_body and previous_failure and invoking assess_node().
glossary.previous_failure: String representing the last error from a failed node attempt, sourced from error_tracker and passed to assess_node() for re-assessment context.
glossary.session_runner_factory: Closure in engine/run.py that constructs AssessmentManager and supplies the configured Anthropic client.
glossary.starting_tier: Constructor parameter on EscalationLadder (from spec #14) that sets the initial tier from which the ladder begins escalation.
glossary.starting_variant: Constructor parameter on EscalationLadder (from spec #14) that sets the initial variant from which the ladder begins escalation.

requirements.title: ComplexityAssessor class and stateless assessment interface

user_story.goal: assess the complexity of a task node by calling a lightweight LLM and receiving a structured recommendation
user_story.benefit: model tier selection can be upgraded dynamically based on task complexity without blocking dispatch

acceptance_criteria.action: defines the ComplexityRecommendation Protocol with required fields recommended_tier (str), recommended_variant (str or None), and confidence (float)
defines the AssessmentResult frozen dataclass with fields: recommended_tier (str), recommended_variant (str or None), confidence (float), and rationale (str)
accepts an existing Anthropic client instance, configurable assessor_model (default: 'claude-haiku-4-5'), and confidence_threshold (default: 0.6) via its constructor
exposes an async method accepting node_body, archetype, mode, base_tier, base_variant, and optional previous_failure string, and returns an AssessmentResult
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: AssessmentResult dataclass instance with all four fields populated

acceptance_criteria.action: maintains no shared mutable state between calls; concurrent assess() invocations are safe without additional locking
does not instantiate ComplexityAssessor; assess_node() falls back to base_tier/base_variant silently with no log entry emitted

accepts an optional client parameter alongside the existing config parameter; when client is non-None, instantiates ComplexityAssessor passing the client, assessor_model, and confidence_threshold from RoutingConfig

edge_cases.action: skips ComplexityAssessor instantiation; every assess_node() call silently returns base tier/variant with no warning or error log

requirements.title: Assessment prompt structure and structured output validation

user_story.goal: send a well-structured prompt to the LLM and parse and validate the JSON response into an AssessmentResult
user_story.benefit: only valid, complete assessments are used for upgrade decisions, preventing unexpected tier/variant combinations

acceptance_criteria.action: constructs a prompt containing: system role establishing the LLM as a complexity assessor, agent role with archetype and mode, current base_tier/base_variant, full node_body text without truncation, and output instruction requesting JSON matching the AssessmentResult schema
appends failure context to the prompt describing why the previous attempt failed

validates that the LLM JSON response contains all four required fields (recommended_tier, recommended_variant, confidence, rationale); confidence is a float in [0.0, 1.0]; recommended_tier is a recognised ModelTier value (case-sensitive); recommended_variant is null, 'fast', 'standard', or 'extended' (case-sensitive)
enforces a 30-second timeout on the assessment API call via the Anthropic SDK's timeout parameter on the individual API call
performs no concurrency capping; each assess_node() call proceeds independently; rate limit errors from the Anthropic API are treated as assessment failures per the error-handling policy

edge_cases.action: treats the entire response as a parse failure; no partial field salvaging; falls back silently to base_tier/base_variant and logs WARNING with exception details
edge_cases.error_condition: LLM response is malformed JSON, missing required fields, contains out-of-range confidence, or contains unrecognised/wrong-case tier or variant values

edge_cases.action: treats timeout as any other failure; falls back silently to base_tier/base_variant and logs WARNING with exception details
edge_cases.error_condition: API call times out after 30 seconds

edge_cases.action: treats rate limit error as assessment failure; falls back silently to base_tier/base_variant and logs WARNING with exception details
edge_cases.error_condition: Anthropic API returns a rate limit error

user_story.goal: apply a complexity recommendation only as an upgrade, never downgrading below the configured base tier or variant
user_story.benefit: registry defaults act as a guaranteed quality floor that the assessor can only raise, never lower

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts recommendation (ComplexityRecommendation), base_tier (str), base_variant (str or None), and confidence_threshold (float); returns a tuple of (effective_tier, effective_variant)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: tuple[str, str | None] where effective_tier >= base_tier in ModelTier ordering

acceptance_criteria.action: returns (base_tier, base_variant) unchanged; no upgrade is applied
resolves effective tier as max(base_tier, recommendation.recommended_tier) using ModelTier ordering, never returning a tier below base_tier
never changes the variant field; always returns None as the effective variant regardless of recommendation.recommended_variant
treats None recommendation as 'no preference'; returns base_variant unchanged
acceptance_criteria.state: recommendation.recommended_variant is None and base_variant is non-None

acceptance_criteria.action: resolves effective variant as max(base_variant, recommendation.recommended_variant) using VARIANT_ORDER, never returning a variant below base_variant
acceptance_criteria.state: both base_variant and recommendation.recommended_variant are non-None

edge_cases.action: returns base_tier unchanged; upgrade-only logic prevents any downgrade
edge_cases.error_condition: recommendation.recommended_tier is below base_tier in ModelTier ordering

user_story.goal: integrate complexity assessment into the dispatch pipeline via AssessmentManager with dependency-injected Anthropic client
user_story.benefit: assessment is seamlessly wired into dispatch without requiring AssessmentManager to manage its own API client lifecycle

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts node_id (str), archetype (str), mode (str or None), node_body (str or None), previous_failure (str or None, default None), and pre_assessed (AssessedComplexity or None, default None); returns an EscalationLadder
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: EscalationLadder with starting_tier and starting_variant set to effective tier/variant

acceptance_criteria.action: supplies the configured Anthropic client to AssessmentManager via its optional client parameter when constructing the AssessmentManager instance

constructs and returns a new EscalationLadder using starting_tier=effective_tier and starting_variant=effective_variant, with ADVANCED ceiling and the same per-tier retry configuration from RoutingConfig

evaluates assessment eligibility in order: (1) no assessor → base fallback, (2) missing/empty node_body → base fallback with DEBUG log, (3) explicit config override → configured tier/variant with DEBUG log, (4) pre_assessed non-None → adapter + apply_assessment(), (5) LLM assessment → ComplexityAssessor.assess() + apply_assessment()

edge_cases.action: skips assessment entirely; falls back to base tier/variant; logs DEBUG message indicating assessment was skipped due to absent or empty body
edge_cases.error_condition: node_body is None or empty string

requirements.title: Re-assessment on retry with failure context

user_story.goal: re-assess a failed node with the failure reason as additional context and construct a fresh EscalationLadder from the new assessment
user_story.benefit: proactive escalation can be recommended based on failure mode rather than waiting for the ladder to exhaust retries at the current tier

acceptance_criteria.action: discards any existing EscalationLadder for the node; re-assesses with previous_failure appended as context; constructs a new EscalationLadder from the re-assessed effective tier/variant
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: new EscalationLadder with starting_tier/starting_variant from re-assessment
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a node fails and is re-dispatched with a previous_failure string

acceptance_criteria.action: sources previous_failure from the last error string stored in error_tracker in the dispatch layer; passes it to ComplexityAssessor.assess() as the previous_failure argument
uses the same ADVANCED ceiling and the same per-tier retry configuration from RoutingConfig as the original ladder; only starting_tier and starting_variant differ

edge_cases.action: returns new EscalationLadder at base tier/variant; prior retry state is not preserved
edge_cases.error_condition: re-assessment recommends same or lower tier than base due to confidence gate or upgrade-only logic

requirements.title: Skip assessment when explicit config override exists

user_story.goal: bypass LLM assessment when the model tier is already explicitly configured via config resolution layers 1–3
user_story.benefit: explicitly configured tiers are respected without incurring unnecessary assessment API calls

acceptance_criteria.action: walks config resolution layers 1 (mode-level override), 2 (per-archetype override), and 3 (legacy dict override) in order; returns True if any layer returns a non-None value for the given archetype/mode; returns False if all three return None
skips layer 1 (mode-level override check) entirely and proceeds directly to layers 2–3; a None mode never causes layer 1 to return True
skips LLM assessment; uses the explicitly configured tier/variant as the EscalationLadder starting point; logs DEBUG entry with node_id, archetype, mode, and resolved tier
acceptance_criteria.trigger: is_explicitly_configured() returns True for the given archetype/mode

edge_cases.action: returns True immediately if layer 1 yields a non-None value, without checking layers 2–3
edge_cases.trigger: layer 1 check is performed with a non-None mode

user_story.goal: resolve model tier and variant according to a strict five-layer priority order, with explicit overrides always winning over dynamic assessment and registry defaults
user_story.benefit: operators retain full control via explicit configuration while the assessor provides dynamic upgrades only in the absence of explicit settings

acceptance_criteria.action: resolves model tier/variant in strict priority order: (1) mode-level config override, (2) per-archetype config override, (3) legacy dict override, (4) LLM assessment upgrade, (5) archetype registry default
may only upgrade from the archetype registry default floor; it never overrides explicit config overrides set at layers 1–3
serves as the base floor tier/variant used by apply_assessment() when no explicit override exists at layers 1–3 and no LLM assessment upgrade applies

requirements.title: Revised default model assignments in ARCHETYPE_REGISTRY

user_story.goal: have all archetype/mode combinations use updated default tier and variant assignments that reflect quality guarantees and cost-efficiency goals
user_story.benefit: quality-critical modes default to ADVANCED tier while cost-sensitive modes default to STANDARD or SIMPLE, forming the assessment floor

acceptance_criteria.action: assigns coder default to STANDARD / standard; coder (fix) default to STANDARD / standard

assigns reviewer (pre-review) default to ADVANCED / standard; reviewer (drift-review) default to STANDARD / standard; reviewer (audit-review) default to ADVANCED / standard; reviewer (fix-review) default to ADVANCED / standard
assigns verifier default to STANDARD / standard
assigns maintainer (hunt) default to SIMPLE / standard; maintainer (fix-triage) default to STANDARD / standard; maintainer (extraction) default to SIMPLE / standard
applies new defaults immediately with no migration path; all 10 archetype/mode combinations reflect the new assignments at system startup

user_story.goal: extract node_body and previous_failure from the task graph and error_tracker and pass them to assess_node() before launching a node
user_story.benefit: complexity assessment receives the correct task content and failure context without the dispatch layer requiring knowledge of assessment internals

acceptance_criteria.action: extracts node_body from the task graph node via self.get_node(node_id).body and passes it to assess_node()
extracts previous_failure from the error_tracker dict (the same previous_error string used for error feedback in retries); passes None if no prior failure exists for the node
passes both node_body and previous_failure to self._routing.assess_node() along with node_id, archetype, and mode

edge_cases.trigger: no prior failure entry exists in error_tracker for the node

requirements.title: RoutingConfig configuration fields with eager validation

user_story.goal: configure the assessor model and confidence threshold via RoutingConfig with validation at startup
user_story.benefit: invalid configuration values are caught immediately at load time, preventing silent misconfiguration from reaching production

acceptance_criteria.action: adds assessor_model field (str, default 'claude-haiku-4-5') under the [routing] section in config.toml; validated at config load time as a non-empty string
adds confidence_threshold field (float, default 0.6) under the [routing] section; validated at config load time using Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0) or equivalent Clamped annotation

requirements.title: Error handling with silent fallback and structured logging

correctness_properties.title: Quality guarantee: pre-review and audit-review always default to ADVANCED
